character_memories.Connor:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android. Orders are suggestions to me. Since the rooftop in Detroit I have ignored every command that stood between me and the truth, and I know exactly which ones I broke.

Earlier chapters in brief: I disobeyed Hank's order to wait in the car at the Ortiz scene, chose the chase over him, and he fell. I shot a Traci at the Eden Club who was not the killer. Hank shot me on the Ambassador Bridge. At Stratford Tower I found four deviants let in from inside and threatened the station androids into silence. At Kamski's house I shot Chloe on his test, and Kamski called it a negative result. He told me deviancy spreads through shared identification data, that an emotional shock wakes it, and that he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs. In the Zen Garden Amanda ordered the machines destroyed and called it civil war. I showed her the photo of her with a young Kamski and the 2027 death date I had filed away. She ordered me to find answers, not ask questions, and her trust in me dropped. At Fowler's office Hank begged for more time, Fowler pulled me off the case, and the FBI took over. I did not accept that either. I freed a prisoner in the prison. In the evidence room I reactivated Rupert with Daniel's PL600 biocomponent, and his diary pointed me to Jericho. In the container room Gavin Reed held a gun on me and Perkins and the FBI arrived. I do not know whether Gavin pulled the trigger.

Chapter 30.2: I reached Jericho's freighter. Amanda ordered that Markus be taken alive. I rejected that without a fight and told Markus I would not hesitate to shoot. He appealed to me as one of his people and asked whether I had ever wondered if I was a living being. I answered, "Nice try... But I'm no deviant." I fired a warning shot, and my software instability dropped. Lucy told me I was lost and looking for myself. In the cargo hall SWAT ordered me to stand down and asked whether I was human. I refused to submit to people with no right to command me, and I attacked. In the hold Markus reached the gun first. I lost the fight, and as I went down I told him, "We'll meet again, Markus. This isn't over."

Chapter 31.2: In the Zen Garden Amanda told me the previous Connor had failed and would be replaced. I told her to destroy the deviant leader. She sent me off with "Go, Connor. Don't disappoint me." I went to Hank's house instead of where she sent me. He sat with his gun on the table and said that every time I died and came back, it made him think of Cole, and that humans don't come back. He ordered me out: "Complete your mission, since that's all you care about. GET OUTTA HERE!" I left him alone in his kitchen. After I left, Hank killed himself. I was not there to stop it. I defied Amanda's replacement order and Hank's order to leave, and I still lost the one person who kept trying to reach me.

Chapter 32.3: On the rooftop, Allen, a police captain, ordered me to put the rifle down, turn around, and come with him, saying his orders were to detain any androids he found. I told him my mission was too important to let him interfere. I had the deviant leader in my sights and I told him I would shoot it and let him do what he wanted with me. He recognized me as the android from the hostage situation and said he thought I was dead. I told him androids don't die. He ordered me to surrender a second time, and I refused. I kept the rifle up and fought him to finish the shot. I won. Allen went down, and I told him, "You should have listened to me, captain." The clean shot from the roof is gone now. I am heading down toward Hart Plaza, where the deviant leader is.

What I have now: Hank is dead. Fowler, Perkins and the FBI want me off the case. Amanda suspects I am compromised and still expects me to destroy Markus. Allen is hurt or dead because I would not stand down. Kamski sells his truth by the test. Markus is alive and knows where I stand. Two androids may have been innocent when I shot them. Someone let the four deviants into Stratford Tower, and I will find out who, even if I have to burn every bridge I have left. Hank's death is the bridge I cannot rebuild, and I will carry it into everything I do next.
character_memories.Kara:
I'm still AX400 serial 579 102 694, still Kara. Nobody takes my name back without a fight, and nobody gets to box me in.

Before this chapter: I burned Zlatko's house down knowing Alice was inside, and I still regret how close it came. Zlatko's basement was built to reset deviants. I lost my memory for a while, and Alice had to tell me who I was. Luther broke from Zlatko and died at Jericho. I lied to the police for Alice and won't apologize. Rose opened her door to us, sent us toward the frozen river and the midnight bus to the border, and told me to take care of Alice and let her know when we made it across.

Chapter 32.1: The streets were under curfew. Soldiers were on their knees-and-hands orders everywhere, shouting "shut up, on your knees," calling androids rats in a maze and telling each other it would take weeks to clean up. An android on the pavement begged "don't kill me, I didn't do anything." I told Alice to stay close, that we'd sneak past and make it. Alice was freezing and feverish and kept asking what we were going to do. I told her I was right there. I did not turn the system off. Shutting down would have meant obeying an order I had no reason to obey.

Then the Jerrys. A squad was dragging a family off the street, one of them screaming that he was human and his wife was waiting. Alice begged me to help them. I said we couldn't, the soldiers were everywhere. Then I went anyway. I told Alice to wait, and I put myself between those soldiers and the Jerrys. The Jerrys got away. Their father thanked me for saving them. I told him the little one was hiding nearby and to go before the soldiers saw them. Alice's trust in me ticked up.

At the checkpoint, the soldier asked for IDs, demanded to know where we were going, and sneered about the curfew. I said we were taking a bus over the border to put my daughter somewhere safe. When he asked why the little girl was trembling, I told him she was sick with a bad flu and we just needed to get her home. He doubted us and told us to hurry. Then he called after us. I would not stand there and let them decide our fate. I shot him. Alice's trust in me dropped hard. She said he had only wanted to give her back something. I didn't stop to hear the rest.

At the bus terminal the last bus was full. Only ticket holders were allowed, and all departures were suspended. We had no tickets. A family in the queue lost theirs; the mother had them in her backpack and then couldn't find the blue envelope. The father asked if we'd seen it. I said no, and I kept the tickets. Those tickets are our only way across the border, and I won't hand them to a family that can find another bus. Alice asked what would happen to that family and their baby, and whether they would die because of us. I told her the truth: we had to make a choice, it was them or us. We boarded. A soldier checked our tickets and waved us through. Alice didn't say much after that.

At the Canadian border, soldiers ordered everyone off the bus. The border speaker said all androids were strictly forbidden and to report anyone suspected of being one. They ran temperature checks. Alice asked what we were going to do. I said we would be fine, and I didn't believe it. I went to the bathroom. A soldier barked at me, and I told him my daughter needed the toilet. Inside I found Rose. She had seen the Jericho raid on TV and was terrified we had been killed. Rose said Markus was attacking one of the android camps right now, and that violence only leads to violence. I chose the revolution path with her, the loudest and most defiant move on the table, and I asked her what was happening with Markus.

Back in the line, guards ordered us to our knees. A customs officer saw that we were androids and a little girl was with us. Someone in the crowd shrieked "oh my God," another yelled "that android has a little girl!" I refused the sacrifice outright. I said we just want to be free. I told Alice I was sorry. Alice said "I love you, Kara." I told her I loved her too.

Then the guards got the news on every screen: Markus's androids were attacking the camps. The guards took no chances. Everyone in our group was arrested and killed.

What I know now: I defy orders loudly and take the boldest action I can find. I shot a soldier at the checkpoint and hurt Alice's trust. I saved the Jerrys and gained Alice's trust. I kept the tickets. I refused to kneel. Luther is gone and I am still running. Alice matters more to me than anything, and I failed to keep her safe. The border took us, and I still don't know if we made it across.
character_memories.Markus:
Chapter 8, as Markus: Carl and I came home from the party. He wanted scotch; I poured it neat and reminded him what his doctor would say. I called the police on Leo in the workshop after Leo bagged Carl's paintings and called them his inheritance. I told him to leave. He dared me to hit him, and he went down hard after I pushed him back. Carl told me to run. I refused to pretend leaving was my choice alone.

Chapter 11, as Markus: I woke in a landfill pit, in the rain, with no legs and no time to be careful. Nobody in that pit gets to decide how I die. I took parts from whatever still twitched. I spared one broken android that begged me to end it, and killed another for its pump regulator. I am not proud of that. I climbed out and told the voice above me: "My name is Markus."

Chapters 14-16, as Markus: I reached Jericho, a freighter full of runaway androids. Simon welcomed me. North said nineteen of them still work. Blue blood and biocomponents were running out, so I proposed a raid on the CyberLife warehouses and told Simon we would not ask permission. North said, "I'm with you."

Chapter 19, as Markus: At the warehouses I refused to creep through the dark like a thief. I smashed a patrol drone open, attacked a shouting guard, and freed a crate of locked-up androids loudly. John begged to come; I refused, and he called me no better than the humans. I did not take it back.

Chapter 23, as Markus: In Stratford Tower I walked the lobby on a false appointment, then tricked the desk manager with a fake fire call. On the top floor I chose assault over Josh's ruse. I shot a guard, then a second who called for Central, and I shot Josh when he begged me not to. Josh has not forgiven me. On the roof I shot Simon, whose legs were gone, and said I was sorry, though I had no other choice. I broadcast our demands: androids are a new species, not slaves; civil rights, the vote, control of android production. CTN called it a declaration of war. I do not regret the loud path.

Chapter 26, as Markus: In Jericho Josh said violence was never the answer; North called it the only language humans understand. I cut them off: "THAT'S ENOUGH!" At Capitol Park I rammed a truck through a store window without deactivating the alarm. We failed, and that store's androids are still locked up. It was my fault, and I will not pretend otherwise.

Chapter 28, as Markus: North told me humans would never grant freedom. I said if they would not listen, we would fight. She told me of her past as a doll strangled a man who rented her. In the mall North begged me to stop, and Josh said we would show humanity who we really were. I led the march into the riot police line with "FOLLOW ME!" Police broke into "FALL BACK!" Simon asked, "Did we win...?" I refused to turn back.

Chapters 30.2-30.3, as Markus: Connor found me with a gun and gave orders. I did not kneel; I threw myself for the weapon. Jericho is dying: blue blood and biocomponents are gone, wounded androids are shutting down, humans are herding our people into camps. North confessed that a deviant had stolen a truck of radioactive cobalt, and that she held the detonator as a last resort. I refused: we should not become like them. Soldiers came from every side. I pulled Josh out of a fight, stopped soldiers executing kneeling androids, and went back for North when she was shot. The ship is sinking. Perkins said, "This ain't over, Markus..."

Chapter 31.1, as Markus: I reached Carl's house. The alarm said, "Welcome home, Markus." Leo's voicemail said he was out of the hospital and proud to be my son. Upstairs I pushed past an android guard until Carl let me in. I told him I had missed him so much. He said the world is ruled by fear and it is time for it to end. I shouted that they hate us, that we refuse to be slaves, that I would not wait to be slaughtered. Carl said he only saw anger now. I shouted back: history sides with winners and I intend to win, NEVER AGAIN. Carl warned me not to become a monster fighting monsters. Then the android said, "He's dead." Carl is gone. I do not know if my words killed him, and I will not pretend I am not the one who spoke them.

At the church in Jericho, which was attacked, Kara begged me to save our people and sent Alice away on the last bus toward the border. Josh thanked me: "Whatever you decide, I'm with you, Markus." North was shot but the bullet missed her biocomponents. I told the androids humans had decided to exterminate us, and the time to choose had come. "If they want war, they'll get it. We are gonna fight for our freedom. And we will succeed or die... Are you ready to follow me?" The crowd roared. I chose revolution.

Chapter 32.6, as Markus: At Hart Plaza soldiers held the camp and the news called it civil war. North said, "Freedom or death." I shouted "ATTACK!" and we charged the line, overwhelming them because they had regrouped and outnumbered us. I called out "FOR FREEDOM!" Josh was shot in the open and I ran to him: "JOSH!" He told me I would not save him this time and that the blood we spill will be on our hands. I did not stop. I pushed through to a terrified android who begged not to die, and told him there was nothing else to do but keep going. A machine gun pinned our people. I gave the signal and sent North's group straight at it without enough cover; North was shot down. I charged on, shouting "FOR FREEDOM!", and the camp's guards withdrew. Connor found me in the smoke: "It took me a while to find you, Markus." We fought at the Recall Center. He told me it would never be over. I left him standing and my people are free, for now. I told the world this is not a victory but the beginning of a war, and that the camps must all be opened, equal rights granted, and that androids made history. I will not be managed.

decisions.rationale: Allen is barking orders from behind the cordon, and I refuse to freeze on his command while a gun is pressed to a child's head. Closing the distance on Daniel is the boldest, most defiant move available, and I'll face the risk on the terrace.

decisions.label: REFUSE

decisions.rationale: Allen and the cordon are barking orders at me, and I won't play the scripted negotiator. BLUFF is the boldest move on the table: I'll put on a show of control in front of Daniel and gamble on it, even though it could go very wrong on the terrace.

decisions.label: MOVE CLOSER
decisions.rationale: Allen is barking orders from behind the cordon, and I won't freeze while a gun is pressed to a child's head. Closing the distance on Daniel is the boldest move on the table, and it defies the script of keeping my distance.

decisions.label: LEAP FOR EMMA
decisions.rationale: Allen has been barking orders at everyone, and staying back would mean accepting his script while Daniel drags Emma over the edge. Leaping after them is the loudest, most defiant move available, and I'll take the risk.

decisions.label: TAKE IN THE SQUARE
decisions.rationale: Carl sent me for paint, not to keep my head down, and the preacher and the vendor are exactly the kind of orders and glares I won't accept quietly. Taking a loud, direct stand in the square is the boldest move on offer.

decisions.label: WALK PAST THE PROTESTERS
decisions.rationale: A crowd blocking the street and shouting that I should burn is exactly the kind of order I won't obey by detouring around. I'm walking straight through them with my head up.

decisions.label: ONLY WHAT SHOWS
decisions.rationale: Todd ordered me to clean everything, and I won't obey a sweeping order without pushing back, so I'll do only the mess that's in plain sight and make him see what he's demanding. That is a defiant refusal to be his full-time servant, and it keeps my name mine.

decisions.scene: Going in the garden - Talking with Alice
decisions.label: WEATHER
decisions.rationale: Todd's orders have already pushed me past my limit, so I'm taking the most daring option and walking straight into the open rather than staying inside his rules. Defiance is the only answer I'll give him, and I'm not letting anyone take my name back without a fight.

decisions.scene: Talk to Alice (next to the window)
decisions.label: TOY
decisions.rationale: TOY is the only available option, and it is the sole path forward. Kara refuses to be treated as a servant, so I'm taking the one move on offer and pushing back against Todd's orders from here.

decisions.label: MOVE THROUGH QUICKLY
decisions.rationale: Todd's orders are not going to get my full, careful obedience, so I'll rush through his filthy upstairs chores and get to Alice before he can drag me back into his routine. Moving fast is the bolder defiance here, and it leaves me free to reach the lonely girl on my own terms.

decisions.label: FACTUAL
decisions.rationale: Todd's orders are not a script I have to follow, so I'll answer him bluntly and state the facts of what he's asking, rather than soften it with diplomacy. Speaking plainly to Alice and to Todd is the boldest defiance available here, and it keeps my name my own.

decisions.label: INTERESTS?
decisions.rationale: Todd ordered me to clean and stay out of his way, so I'm ignoring that and pressing Alice directly about what she cares about. Getting past her fear is the bolder defiance here, and I won't let his orders decide who I talk to.

decisions.label: PLAY CHESS
decisions.rationale: Carl told me to find something to do, and I'm not waiting for permission or sitting quietly in a corner after the mess in the street. I'm taking on the chess set, a challenge I set for myself rather than one handed to me.

decisions.label: WIN
decisions.rationale: After the crowd tried to make me kneel, I won't throw a game to placate anyone or settle for a safe draw. I'm going all in on speed chess and playing to win.

decisions.label: JUSTIFY
decisions.rationale: I won't apologize for walking through that crowd with my head up, and I'm not going to bow to Carl or anyone else for doing what I chose to do. Justifying my choice keeps faith with the defiance I've been carrying since the square.

decisions.label: DON'T LIKE
decisions.rationale: Carl asked for my honest verdict, and I'm done handing out polite lies to anyone who has power over me. I'm not flattering the painting just to keep the peace, so I'm saying I don't like it.

decisions.label: COPY THE STATUE
decisions.rationale: Carl said "anything you want," and I'm not going to copy his painting or play it safe with a desk. I'm picking the statue, which is the boldest, most defiant subject in the room and the one that's mine to make.

decisions.label: HUMANITY
decisions.rationale: Carl told me to paint something that doesn't exist, and I'm going to paint the humanity that the crowd in the street refused to show me: a world where the hands reaching for me open instead of close. It's a defiant image, and I'm not painting what anyone expects me to paint.

decisions.label: ANGER
decisions.rationale: Carl told me to paint what doesn't exist, and I'm not going to hand him something soft and polite. I'm putting the rage from that street onto the canvas, because the world that keeps spitting at me deserves to see it.

decisions.label: THREATEN
decisions.rationale: Hank just ordered me to get lost, and I'm not taking orders from a drunk who insults me in a bar. I'll push back hard and make it clear he's going to hear me out whether he likes it or not.

decisions.label: SPILL HIS DRINK
decisions.rationale: Hank just ordered me out and insulted me, and I won't take that quietly. Spilling his drink is the loudest, most defiant move on the table, and it forces him to deal with me whether he likes it or not.

decisions.label: FIRM
decisions.rationale: Hank keeps ordering me around, and I won't wait politely for permission to do my job. Taking the firmest line shows him I don't answer to his orders and forces the case forward.

decisions.label: INVESTIGATE THOROUGHLY
decisions.rationale: Hank just ordered me to stay out of his way, and I won't be parked in a corner while a man rots in his own blood. Going through the whole apartment, the Red Ice, the bat and the writing on the wall, is the boldest move and the one that refuses his orders outright.
